title: Limitations — Flight Compartment Windows and Window Heating

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew limitations for the flight compartment windows, covering window heating availability, the acceptable state of the pane before departure and the speed restriction after a heating failure.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the limitations applicable to the flight compartment windows and their heating, and the crew assessment of pane condition before departure.
sections.description: Each flight compartment window is heated to keep it clear and to maintain its impact resistance. Heating is controlled automatically and its state is shown on the systems page. A window without heating retains its structural strength but not its published impact resistance at high speed, which is why a speed restriction applies after a heating failure rather than a prohibition on flight. The panes themselves are inspected by maintenance, but the crew assesses the visible condition before departure: delamination visible at an edge, an arc mark at a terminal or moisture trapped between the layers are all reportable and may make the window unserviceable. Small surface marks on the outer face that do not obstruct the view are acceptable and are managed by maintenance.
sections.crew_procedure: During the preflight check, look along each windshield and side window for edge delamination, arc marking at the terminals and trapped moisture, and report anything found. Confirm the window heating state on the systems page. If a heating channel fails in flight, apply the speed restriction in the limitations table for the remainder of the flight and record the failure in the technical log.
sections.limitation_note: With one window heating channel inoperative, the maximum airspeed below 10 000 feet is restricted in accordance with the limitations table. Departure with delamination visible at a pane edge is not permitted.

type_data.crew_action: Check pane condition and heating state before departure; apply the speed restriction after a heating failure.
